claim: Segmentation of the axial skeleton in amniotes depends on the segmentation clock, which patterns the paraxial mesoderm and the sclerotome.
source: Segmentation of the axial skeleton in amniotes depends on the segmentation clock, which patterns the paraxial mesoderm and the sclerotome.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific understanding about amniote development, drawing on general knowledge in the field.

claim: The role of the sclerotome in establishing the axial skeleton in teleosts is unclear.
source: While the segmentation clock clearly operates in teleosts, the role of the sclerotome in establishing the axial skeleton is unclear.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of knowledge and uncertainty in the field regarding teleost development.

claim: Severe disruption of zebrafish paraxial segmentation results in a largely normal segmentation process of the chordacentra.
source: We severely disrupt zebrafish paraxial segmentation, yet observe a largely normal segmentation process of the chordacentra.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental observations presented in the manuscript.

claim: Axial entpd5+ notochord sheath cells are responsible for chordacentrum mineralization.
source: We demonstrate that axial entpd5+ notochord sheath cells are responsible for chordacentrum mineralization, and serve as a marker for axial segmentation.
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated through experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: entpd5 expression and centrum formation show some plasticity and can respond to myotome pattern.
source: While autonomous within the notochord sheath, entpd5 expression and centrum formation show some plasticity and can respond to myotome pattern.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on experimental observations.

claim: The behavior of notochord segmentation is not consistent with a clock-type mechanism in the notochord.
source: This behavior is not consistent with a clock-type mechanism in the notochord.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations and analysis presented in the study.

claim: In amniotes, all elements of the vertebral column as well as adjacent muscle and sub-cutis derive from transient embryonic segmented structures termed somites.
source: In amniotes, such as mammals and birds, all these elements as well as adjacent muscle and sub-cutis derive from transient embryonic segmented structures termed somites.
evidence: This is established knowledge about amniote development.

claim: The sclerotome occupies the bulk of the somite, whereas skin and muscle are derived from the smaller derma-myotome.
source: The sclerotome occupies the bulk of the somite, whereas skin and muscle are derived from the smaller derma-myotome.
evidence: This is established knowledge about somite composition.

claim: Somites are formed rhythmically and sequentially along the embryonic axis in a process governed by a multicellular, genetic oscillator termed the segmentation clock.
source: In all vertebrates, somites are formed rhythmically and sequentially along the embryonic axis in a process governed by a multicellular, genetic oscillator termed the segmentation clock.
evidence: This is established knowledge about somitogenesis across vertebrates.

claim: Sequential waves of oscillating gene expression move through the precursor cells of the pre-somitic mesoderm (PSM) from the posterior to the anterior, where their arrest prefigures the timing and location of each newly forming somite boundary.
source: Sequential waves of oscillating gene expression move through the precursor cells of the pre-somitic mesoderm (PSM) from the posterior to the anterior, where their arrest prefigures the timing and location of each newly forming somite boundary (Masamizu et al., 2006; Aulehla et al., 2008; Soroldoni et al., 2014; Shimojo and Kageyama, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Members of the Hes/her family of transcriptional repressors appear to form a core negative feedback loop in all species examined.
source: The segmentation clock contains a network of oscillating genes that shows differences between species, but members of the Hes/her family of transcriptional repressors appear to form a core negative feedback loop in all species examined (Krol et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Mutations that disrupt the mouse clock (e.g. Hes7) cause defective somitogenesis and corresponding defects to the centra and arches of the spinal column.
source: Mutations that disrupt the mouse clock (e.g. Hes7 [Bessho et al., 2001]) cause defective somitogenesis and corresponding defects to the centra and arches of the spinal column.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Surgical perturbation of somites in chick embryos produce defects in the centra and arches.
source: Similarly, surgical perturbation of somites in chick embryos produce defects in the centra and arches (Stern and Keynes, 1987; Aoyama and Asamoto, 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Engineered changes to the mouse clock that shorten the period of oscillations correspondingly produce more vertebral bodies.
source: Engineered changes to the mouse clock that shorten the period of oscillations correspondingly produce more vertebral bodies (Harima et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: In zebrafish and salmon, the notochord and not the sclerotome is the initial source of bone matrix for chordacentra formation.
source: It has been proposed that in the teleosts zebrafish (Fleming et al., 2004) and salmon (Grotmol et al., 2003; Wang et al., 2013) the notochord and not the sclerotome is the initial source of bone matrix for chordacentra formation
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In other teleost species, classical sclerotome-derived osteoblasts have been suggested as the main drivers of chordacentrum formation.
source: while in other teleost species the classical sclerotome-derived osteoblasts have been suggested as the main drivers of chordacentrum formation (Inohaya et al., 2007; Renn et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Chordacentra are first observed as they mineralize as rings around the notochord, forming sequentially along the axis in a process that begins several days after somitogenesis and muscle segmentation is completed and lasts several weeks.
source: Chordacentra are first observed as they mineralize as rings around the notochord, forming sequentially along the axis in a process that begins several days after somitogenesis and muscle segmentation is completed and lasts several weeks.
evidence: This is a description of the developmental process based on established knowledge.

claim: The zebrafish fused somites/tbx6 (fss) mutant has unsegmented paraxial mesoderm and ectopically positioned neural and hemal arches, but was reported to form normal vertebral centra.
source: The zebrafish fused somites/tbx6 (fss) mutant, which has unsegmented paraxial mesoderm, has ectopically positioned neural and hemal arches, but was reported to form normal vertebral centra (Fleming et al., 2004; van Eeden et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A segmented sclerotome is necessary for proper arch development, but not for segmentation of the chordacentra.
source: This suggests that a segmented sclerotome is necessary for proper arch development, but not for segmentation of the chordacentra.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited observations about the tbx6 mutant.

claim: The zebrafish hes6 mutant forms somites more slowly than wild type and makes correspondingly fewer centra.
source: However, the zebrafish hes6 mutant, which forms somites more slowly than wild type, makes correspondingly fewer centra (Schröter and Oates, 2010)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The segmentation clock can influence vertebral patterning.
source: suggesting that the segmentation clock can influence vertebral patterning.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited observation about the hes6 mutant.

claim: The tbx6 mutant retains a dynamic segmentation clock in the posterior of the PSM, but specifically fails to output the clock's information in the anterior PSM.
source: Indeed, gene expression studies suggest that the tbx6 mutant retains a dynamic segmentation clock in the posterior of the PSM, but specifically fails to output the clock's information in the anterior PSM (van Eeden et al., 1998; Holley et al., 2000; Nikaido et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The zebrafish segmentation clock's core pacemaker circuit consists of her1, her7 and hes6, which display partial and overlapping redundancy.
source: The zebrafish segmentation clock's core pacemaker circuit consists of her1, her7 and hes6, which display partial and overlapping redundancy (Schröter et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: A her1;her7 double mutant was generated by injecting a TALEN construct directed against her1 in the her7 mutant.
source: We generated a her1;her7 double mutant by injecting a TALEN construct directed against her1 in the her7 mutant (Choorapoikayil et al., 2012)
evidence: This describes a method used in the study.

claim: A novel hes6 mutation was generated using a TALEN approach.
source: and a novel hes6 mutation also using a TALEN approach (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes a method used in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: The her1 TALEN allele has two consecutive premature stop codons (TAA TAA).
source: The her1 TALEN allele has two consecutive premature stop codons (TAA TAA).
evidence: This is data from the genetic analysis of the mutant.

claim: The predicted Her1 protein from the TALEN-induced mutation lacks the basic DNA-binding domain and the HLH dimerization domain, suggesting that the protein product has no functionality.
source: The predicted Her1 protein from the TALEN-induced mutation lacks the basic DNA-binding domain and the HLH dimerization domain, suggesting that the protein product has no functionality.
evidence: This is an inference based on the genetic data and knowledge of protein structure-function relationships.

claim: The hu2526 allele is a her7 null mutant resulting from a stop codon in the HLH domain.
source: It has been previously shown that the hu2526 allele is a her7 null mutant resulting from a stop codon in the HLH domain (Schröter et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The phenotype of her1;her7 double mutants is consistent with the phenotype of her1, her7 double morphants and also of the b567 deletion allele.
source: Importantly, the phenotype of her1;her7 double mutants is consistent with the phenotype of her1, her7 double morphants and also of the b567 deletion allele (Henry et al., 2002; Oates and Ho, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research and comparison of phenotypes.

claim: In tbx6−/−, her7 still oscillated posteriorly, but mespb was not expressed.
source: In tbx6−/−, her7 still oscillated posteriorly (Figure 1B,B´), but mespb was not expressed (Figure 1F), as expected (Oates et al., 2005; Durbin et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures and citations to previous research.

claim: In her1;her7 double mutants, her7 was expressed throughout the PSM but lacked oscillatory waves, and mespb expression in the anterior PSM occurred in a diffuse domain, lacking segmented stripes.
source: In her1;her7 double mutants, her7 was expressed throughout the PSM (Figure 1C,C'), but lacked oscillatory waves, and mespb expression in the anterior PSM occurred in a diffuse domain, lacking segmented stripes (Figure 1G; Figure 1—figure supplement 3B), consistent with previous results using anti-sense knock-down reagents (Oates and Ho, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures and citations to previous research.

claim: Expression of other markers of segmental patterning in the anterior PSM (papc, ripply1, ripply2) also lacked segmental stripes in her1−/−;her7−/−.
source: Expression of other markers of segmental patterning in the anterior PSM (papc, ripply1, ripply2) also lacked segmental stripes (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C–H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: In her1−/−;her7−/−, the segmentation clock is severely disrupted throughout the PSM, and a correspondingly disordered, non-segmental output is made in the anterior PSM.
source: This reveals that in her1−/−;her7−/−, the segmentation clock is severely disrupted throughout the PSM, and that a correspondingly disordered, non-segmental output is made in the anterior PSM.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Triple mutants for her1, her7 and hes6 have the same expression patterns as her1;her7 double mutants for all markers analyzed.
source: Triple mutants for her1, her7 and hes6 have the same expression patterns as her1;her7 double mutants for all markers analyzed (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: In her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/−, her7 expression in the posterior PSM lacked oscillatory waves and neither her7 nor mespb was expressed in the anterior PSM.
source: Finally, we examined her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− and found that her7 expression in the posterior PSM lacked oscillatory waves and neither her7 (Figure 1D,D') nor mespb (Figure 1H) was expressed in the anterior PSM.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− resembles the simple addition of the tbx6 and her1;her7 double mutant phenotypes; namely a severely disrupted segmentation clock that lacks any output in the anterior.
source: From these results we conclude that her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− resembles the simple addition of the tbx6 and her1;her7 double mutant phenotypes; namely a severely disrupted segmentation clock that lacks any output in the anterior.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Somite boundaries could not be discerned in tbx6 or her1;her7;tbx6 triple mutants.
source: Somite boundaries could not be discerned in tbx6 or her1;her7;tbx6 triple mutants (Figure 1J,J' and L,L').
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: In her1−/−;her7−/−, partial boundaries were visible, but were lacking regular shape and periodic arrangement.
source: In her1−/−;her7−/− (Figure 1K,K'), partial boundaries were visible, but were lacking regular shape and periodic arrangement.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Periodic morphology is disrupted in the mutant paraxial mesoderm.
source: This indicates that periodic morphology is disrupted in the mutant paraxial mesoderm.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The normal periodic pattern of muscle pioneers is lost in tbx6−/−, her1−/−;her7−/− and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/−.
source: The normal periodic pattern is lost in tbx6−/− (Figure 1N,N'), her1−/−;her7−/− (Figure 1O,O') and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− (Figure 1P,P'), indicating that although these cell types are present in these mutants, there is no overt segmental pattern emerging directly from the PSM.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Myotome boundaries in the paraxial mesoderm are disrupted to differing degrees of severity depending on the genotype.
source: We observed strong disruption of periodic myotome boundaries in all mutants (Figure 2B–D' and Figure 2—figure supplement 2), with the severity in tbx6−/− and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− (Figure 2B,B' and D,D') equivalent, and stronger than that found in her1−/−;her7−/− (Figure 2C,C').
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The short and scattered boundary fragments visible in her1−/−;her7−/− correlate with earlier expression of mespb and partial somite boundaries in the PSM.
source: The short and scattered boundary fragments visible in her1−/−;her7−/− (Figure 2C') correlate with earlier expression of mespb and partial somite boundaries in the PSM (Figure 1G, Figure 1K,K')
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing data shown in different figures.

claim: The short and scattered boundary fragments in her1−/−;her7−/− may arise from a secondary morphogenetic effect of elongating muscle fibers, some of which are lost in the absence of fss/tbx6.
source: and may arise from a secondary morphogenetic effect of elongating muscle fibers (van Eeden et al., 1998), some of which are lost in the absence of fss/tbx6 (Windner et al., 2015).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Centra are well-formed in tbx6−/−.
source: Centra are well-formed in tbx6−/− (n = 10) (F), while neural and hemal arches are often fused (F´).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Centra are well-formed in her1−/−;her7−/− and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/−.
source: Centra are also well-formed in her1−/−;her7−/− (n = 14) (G,G') and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− (n = 15) (H,H').
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Occasional defects occur in mutant centra, seen as smaller vertebrae or as fusions of two vertebrae.
source: Occasional defects occur, seen as smaller vertebrae (arrowhead in F'), or as fusions of two vertebrae (arrowheads in G' and H').
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The majority of centra in her1−/−;her7−/− and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− adults were remarkably well-formed.
source: However, the majority of centra in her1−/−;her7−/− and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− adults were remarkably well-formed, defined as being cleanly separated from neighboring centra and similar to wildtype in their basic hourglass shape (Figure 2F–H).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: All centra were well-formed in all her1, her7 and hes6 hetero- and homozygotes, in all heterozygous double and triple crosses, and in hes6;her7 double mutants.
source: Furthermore, we confirmed that all centra were well-formed in all her1, her7 and hes6 hetero- and homozygotes (Hanisch et al., 2013), in all heterozygous double and triple crosses, and in hes6;her7 double mutants.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study and a citation to previous research.

claim: Centra were well-formed in mutants where the segmentation clock's oscillating cells slowly desynchronize due to a loss in Delta-Notch signaling, such as in beamter/deltaC and after eight/deltaD.
source: In addition, centra were also well-formed in mutants where the segmentation clock's oscillating cells slowly desynchronize due to a loss in Delta-Notch signaling, such as in beamter/deltaC and after eight/deltaD (Durbin et al., 2000) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures and a citation to previous research.

claim: The segmentation clock activity remaining in the posterior PSM of tbx6 mutant embryos is not the cause of the well-formed vertebral centra observed in tbx6−/− adults.
source: Thus, the segmentation clock activity remaining in the posterior PSM of tbx6 mutant embryos is not the cause of the well-formed vertebral centra observed in tbx6−/− adults.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Localized defects such as a bend in the axis or occasional malformations and fusion of neighboring centra were observed scattered along every her1;her7 and her1;hes6 double mutant, and her1;her7;hes6 and her1;her7;tbx6 triple mutant skeletons, as well as in 80% of tbx6−/− skeletons.
source: However, in some mutant combinations we did observe localized defects, such as a bend in the axis or occasional malformations and fusion of neighboring centra, scattered along every her1;her7 and her1;hes6 double mutant, and her1;her7;hes6 and her1;her7;tbx6 triple mutant skeletons, as well as in 80% of tbx6−/− skeletons (Figure 2F–H and Figure 2—figure supplement 4R,U).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Previous reports of normal segmentation of the centra in tbx6−/− were incomplete.
source: This shows that previous reports of normal segmentation of the centra in tbx6−/− were incomplete (Fleming et al., 2004; van Eeden et al., 1996)
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the current study's findings and citations to previous research.

claim: In the absence of periodic order in the early paraxial mesoderm, formation of the centra is error-prone.
source: and indicates that in the absence of periodic order in the early paraxial mesoderm, formation of the centra is error-prone.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Formation of periodic chordacentra may arise from a separate segmentation mechanism intrinsic to the notochord.
source: Given the proximity of the developing chordacentra to the notochord, and the suggestion that the notochord serves as a linear template for the vertebral column (Gray et al., 2014), our findings argue instead that formation of periodic chordacentra may arise from a separate segmentation mechanism intrinsic to the notochord.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental findings and a citation to previous research.

claim: Secreted Entpd5 has previously been shown to be required for bone formation in zebrafish, and to be co-expressed with osterix (osx) in craniofacial osteoblasts.
source: Secreted Entpd5 has previously been shown to be required for bone formation in zebrafish, and to be co-expressed with osterix (osx) in craniofacial osteoblasts (Huitema et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: entpd5 promoter activity shows a striking segmented pattern in the sheath cells along the notochord.
source: When examining entpd5 promoter activity outside the craniofacial area, we observed a striking segmented pattern in the sheath cells along the notochord (Figure 3A)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The segmented entpd5 pattern is observed well before the onset of chordacentrum mineralization is first observed in the anterior notochord at 6 dpf.
source: well before the onset of chordacentrum mineralization is first observed in the anterior notochord at 6 dpf (Morin-Kensicki et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Photoconversion at 3 dpf of Kaede expressed from an entpd5:kaede transgene showed that entpd5 rings arise from an earlier ubiquitous expression domain by de novo synthesis.
source: Photoconversion at 3 dpf (Figure 3B) of Kaede expressed from an entpd5:kaede transgene showed that these rings arise from an earlier ubiquitous expression domain by de novo synthesis (Figure 3C)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: entpd5 is the earliest axial segmented marker known for zebrafish.
source: making entpd5 the earliest axial segmented marker known for zebrafish.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: entpd5 is segmentally expressed first in the dorsal region of the sheath cell layer at the anterior, and new, periodically forming rings of entpd5 expression formed sequentially from anterior to posterior along the axis.
source: We found entpd5 to be segmentally expressed first in the dorsal region of the sheath cell layer at the anterior, and new, periodically forming rings of entpd5 expression formed sequentially from anterior to posterior along the axis (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: entpd5+ sheath cells precisely predicted the position of the mineralized chordacentra and were located centrally to the mineralized matrix.
source: entpd5+ sheath cells precisely predicted the position of the mineralized chordacentra and were located centrally to the mineralized matrix as revealed by co-staining with AR (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: In classical osteoblasts, entpd5 is co-expressed with the osteoblast regulator osterix/Sp7.
source: In classical osteoblasts (cells able to produce bone matrix), as are found in the cleithrum or parasphenoid bones of the head, entpd5 is co-expressed with the osteoblast regulator osterix/Sp7 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Within the developing vertebral column, osterix expression is first observed after 17 dpf when neural and hemal arches begin to form.
source: whereas within the developing vertebral column, osterix expression is first observed after 17 dpf when neural and hemal arches begin to form (Spoorendonk et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: entpd5 mutants form normally segmented osteoid, but do not mineralize it.
source: entpd5 mutants form normally segmented osteoid, but do not mineralize it (Huitema et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: osterix mutants have normal entpd5 expression and ossification in the notochord, but reduced ossification in the head.
source: In contrast, osterix mutants have normal entpd5 expression and ossification in the notochord, but reduced ossification in the head (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: In wildtype larvae, entpd5+ segments are established in an anterior to posterior progression at a rate of ~1.5 per day.
source: In wildtype larvae (Figure 4A; Figure 4—figure supplement 1), entpd5+ segments are established in an anterior to posterior progression at a rate of ~1.5 per day
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The first two entpd5+ segments (part of the Weberian apparatus) appear dorsally at first and are completed 4–6 days later.
source: with the exception of the first two segments (part of the Weberian apparatus) which appear dorsally at first and are completed 4–6 days later.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: As each chordacentrum matured, entpd5 expression was down-regulated in the center and was retained at the distal edges of each element.
source: As each chordacentrum matured, entpd5 expression was down-regulated in the center and was retained at the distal edges of each element, as illustrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The process of entpd5 down-regulation in the center of chordacentra began around 15 dpf in the anterior chordacentra, and sequentially progressed posterior-wards along the axis.
source: This process began around 15 dpf in the anterior chordacentra, and sequentially progressed posterior-wards along the axis.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: In tbx6−/−, her1−/−;her7−/−, and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− mutants, the chordacentra formed in an anterior to posterior direction as in wild type.
source: In the case of tbx6 (n = 4), her1;her7 (n = 4), her1;her7;tbx6 (n = 4) and hes6 (n = 6) mutants (Figure 4B–D, Figure 5A and B, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 5), the chordacentra formed in an anterior to posterior direction as in .
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Two types of defects were observed in mutant chordacentra: a ring was initially not formed, leaving a transient gap which was then modified by the subsequent intercalation of a new entpd5 expression ring two or more days later.
source: However, we observed two types of defects: in the first, a ring was initially not formed, leaving a transient gap (Figure 5A and longer spaces in the kymograms), which was then modified by the subsequent intercalation of a new entpd5 expression ring two or more days later (segment 1' in Figure 5A, 19 dpf).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The intercalated ring was thinner than neighboring elements, likely reflecting an earlier stage in ring development, and remained smaller and distinct from neighboring segments.
source: The intercalated ring was thinner than neighboring elements, likely reflecting an earlier stage in ring development, and remained smaller and distinct from neighboring segments.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: In the second type of defect, a ring was added (on schedule or out of schedule) in the middle of a normal intervertebral distance, creating a distance shorter than expected between two rings.
source: In the second type of defect, a ring was added (on schedule or out of schedule) in the middle of a normal intervertebral distance, creating a distance shorter than expected between two rings.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: In the second type of defect, the notochord sheath cells of the small segment fused with one or two of its neighboring segments.
source: In this case, the notochord sheath cells of the small segment fused with one or two of its neighboring segments (Figure 5B, black boxes in kymograms).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: When two sequential defects are inserted by any of the two processes described, a transient bending of the axis was observed, which was later modified by fusing segments or leaving two or three contiguous small vertebrae.
source: In the cases where two sequential defects are inserted by any of the two processes described above, we observed a transient bending of the axis, which was later modified by fusing segments or leaving two or three contiguous small vertebrae (Figure 4C, her1−/−;her7−/− kymogram and Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The phenotypic defects observed are different to the scoliosis phenotypes reported in mutant leviathan/col8a1a animals with defects in collagen deposition or in mutant stocksteif/cyp26b1 animals with increased retinoic acid levels.
source: The phenotypic defects we see are different to the scoliosis phenotypes reported in mutant leviathan/col8a1a animals with defects in collagen deposition (Gray et al., 2014) or in mutant stocksteif/cyp26b1 animals with increased retinoic acid levels (Spoorendonk et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In leviathan/col8a1a and stocksteif/cyp26b1 mutants, the first pattern of mineralization appears correctly segmented, and defects arise because of axial bending of the notochord and bone overgrowth, respectively.
source: In these cases, the first pattern of mineralization appears correctly segmented, and defects arise because of axial bending of the notochord and bone overgrowth, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The initial emergence of defective entpd5+ rings was directly observed, suggesting that the periodic patterning of the notochord has been affected.
source: In contrast, we have directly observed the initial emergence of defective entpd5+ rings, suggesting that the periodic patterning of the notochord has been affected.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Segment defects in the paraxial mesoderm occur sequentially along the axis, consistent with a disrupted clock-type mechanism.
source: Segment defects in the paraxial mesoderm occur sequentially along the axis, consistent with a disrupted clock-type mechanism.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The intercalation defects observed in the mutant axes form out of schedule with the sequence of notochord segmentation.
source: In contrast, the intercalation defects observed in the mutant axes form out of schedule with the sequence of notochord segmentation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The distance preceding an intercalation was either similar to or larger than expected from the controls, but never smaller.
source: The distance preceding an intercalation was either similar to or larger than expected from the controls, but never smaller (n = 18, 1.4 ± 0.3 fold increase, mean ± SD).
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: The intercalatory rings formed at a range of distances from their earlier neighbors, suggesting that the defects arise as a response to an error in positioning the earlier rings and are not a simple delay in entpd5 expression.
source: Thus, the intercalatory rings formed at a range of distances from their earlier neighbors, suggesting that the defects arise as a response to an error in positioning the earlier rings and are not a simple delay in entpd5 expression.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The distinctive intercalations are difficult to reconcile with a clock-type mechanism for segmenting the notochord.
source: These distinctive intercalations are difficult to reconcile with a clock-type mechanism for segmenting the notochord.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: hes6 mutants show weak myotome boundary defects in the posterior tail at low penetrance at 1.5 dpf.
source: Previously, it was shown that hes6 mutants show weak myotome boundary defects in the posterior tail at low penetrance at 1.5 dpf (Schröter and Oates, 2010), and the hes6 mutant generated in this paper also show these defects (9/67 (13.4%)).
evidence: This is supported by data from the study and a citation to previous research.

claim: In hes6−/− skeletons, from one to four centra defects, restricted to the caudal vertebrae, were observed in AR stains of adult bone (4/15, 27%) and in entpd5 expression at 28 dpf (8/41, 20%).
source: In hes6−/− skeletons we observed from one to four centra defects, restricted to the caudal vertebrae, in AR stains of adult bone (4/15, 27%) (Figure 6A and B) and in entpd5 expression at 28 dpf (8/41, 20%) (Figure 6C–E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: 2/5 (40%) hes6 mutants with a chordacentra defect revealed by entpd5 expression also presented a myotome defect in the same region.
source: Additional analysis showed that 2/5 (40%) hes6 mutants with a chordacentra defect revealed by entpd5 expression also presented a myotome defect in the same region.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: 60% (3/5) of hes6 mutants with a chordacentra defect had no myotome defect, but still showed a chordacentra defect.
source: The remaining 60% (3/5) had no myotome defect, but still showed a chordacentra defect.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: The partial overlap of myotome and chordacentra defects in hes6 mutants, as well as the coordinated reduction in total myotome and vertebral number, suggests that the pattern of the paraxial mesoderm can influence the segmentation of the notochord.
source: This partial overlap of myotome and chordacentra defects in hes6 mutants, as well as the coordinated reduction in total myotome and vertebral number observed previously (Schröter and Oates, 2010) and in our work suggests that the pattern of the paraxial mesoderm can influence the segmentation of the notochord.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations and a citation to previous research.

claim: A second mechanism for periodic segmentation of the axial skeleton exists in the sheath cells of the zebrafish notochord.
source: In summary, we have proposed a second mechanism for periodic segmentation of the axial skeleton of a vertebrate species, which exists in the sheath cells of the zebrafish notochord.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the experimental findings.

claim: The existence of intercalary defects argues that although there is a sequential generation of periodic entpd5 expression rings, this periodicity does not arise from a clock-type segmentation mechanism as found in the paraxial mesoderm.
source: The existence of intercalary defects argues that although there is a sequential generation of periodic entpd5 expression rings, this periodicity does not arise from a clock-type segmentation mechanism as found in the paraxial mesoderm.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The dynamic mechanism of notochord segmentation is described as a reaction-diffusion process that sweeps down the axis, generating segments autonomously and refining their position using information from the previously segmented myotomes.
source: We have described this dynamic mechanism as a reaction-diffusion process that sweeps down the axis, generating segments autonomously and refining their position using information from the previously segmented myotomes.
evidence: This is a theoretical model proposed to explain the experimental observations.

claim: The zebrafish notochord consists of a core of vacuolated cells responsible for turgor pressure, and an outer, squamous epithelial layer, the sheath cells, that is adjacent to the notochord's basal lamina or sheath, which provides mechanical stability.
source: The zebrafish notochord consists of a core of vacuolated cells responsible for turgor pressure, and an outer, squamous epithelial layer, the sheath cells, that is adjacent to the notochord's basal lamina or sheath, which provides mechanical stability (Melby et al., 1996; Yamamoto et al., 2010) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research and a figure.

claim: entpd5 is expressed in notochord cells, and at 4 dpf, the expression in the axial mesoderm becomes restricted to segmentally organized rings in the notochord sheath cells.
source: but we here show that entpd5 is also expressed in notochord cells (Figure 3), and that, at 4 dpf, the expression in the axial mesoderm becomes restricted to segmentally organized rings in the notochord sheath cells.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: osx is not expressed at early stages in the notochord sheath cells, nor do osx mutants present with an axial mineralization phenotype in zebrafish or Medaka.
source: osx is not expressed at these early stages in the notochord sheath cells, nor do osx mutant present with an axial mineralization phenotype in zebrafish or Medaka (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Yu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures and a citation to previous research.

claim: The osx-, entpd5+ sheath cells are those osteoblasts responsible for initial chordacentra formation.
source: Combined, these results identify the osx-, entpd5+ sheath cells as those osteoblasts responsible for initial chordacentra formation
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The segmental patterning of the notochord is under way by 4 dpf in the sheath cells.
source: and indicate that the segmental patterning of the notochord is under way by 4 dpf in these cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The segmental expression of Entpd5 in the notochord sheath provides the enzymatic activity to mineralize the fibrous sheath of the notochord.
source: Mechanistically, the segmental expression of Entpd5 in the notochord sheath provides the enzymatic activity to mineralize the fibrous sheath of the notochord.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known function of Entpd5 and the experimental observations.

claim: The respective contribution of notochord sheath cells in chordacentrum formation versus sclerotome-derived osteoblast function in centrum formation may be different in other teleost species.
source: It is possible that the respective contribution of notochord sheath cells in chordacentrum formation versus sclerotome-derived osteoblast function in centrum formation is different in other teleost species (Fleming et al., 2015; Yasutake et al., 2004; Kaneko et al., 2016)
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to previous research.

claim: It has been suggested that the chordacentrum is a novelty found only in actinopterygians.
source: From an evolutionary perspective, it has been suggested that the chordacentrum is a novelty found only in actinopterygians (Arratia et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Chordacentrum formation is conserved at least among teleosts.
source: It seems safe to state that chordacentrum formation is conserved at least among teleosts
evidence: This is an inference based on knowledge in the field.

claim: Clock-based mechanisms are involved in body segmentation in vertebrates as well as invertebrates.
source: Recent work has shown that clock-based mechanisms are involved in body segmentation in vertebrates as well as invertebrates (Sarrazin et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Amniotes segmentally pattern their muscles and axial skeletons at the same time during development using the 'segmentation clock'.
source: and there is wide agreement that amniotes segmentally pattern their muscles and axial skeletons at the same time during development using the 'segmentation clock'.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: From fossil and extant taxa it seems likely that neural and hemal arches are evolutionarily older than vertebral bodies.
source: However, from fossil and extant taxa it seems likely that neural and hemal arches are evolutionarily older than vertebral bodies (Cote et al., 2002)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Neural and hemal arches are homologous across vertebrate classes, but vertebral bodies are not.
source: and while these structures are homologous across vertebrate classes (Williams, 1959), vertebral bodies are not.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The phenotype of her1;her7 double mutants is not exacerbated in the further absence of hes6.
source: Analysis using a number of different read-outs demonstrate that the phenotype of her1;her7 double mutants is not exacerbated in the further absence of hes6.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: Strongest disruption of the clock is seen in the case of her1;her7;tbx6 triple mutants.
source: Strongest disruption of the clock is seen in the case of her1;her7;tbx6 triple mutants.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: The mutants used to interfere with the segmentation clock and its output leave the PSM without any overt signs of oscillation or segmental pattern.
source: The mutants we have used to interfere with the segmentation clock and its output leave the PSM without any overt signs of oscillation or segmental pattern.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: The strongest axial phenotype is found in her1−/−;her7−/−, which possesses prominent myotome boundary fragments in the paraxial mesoderm.
source: The strongest axial phenotype is found in her1−/−;her7−/−, which possesses prominent myotome boundary fragments in the paraxial mesoderm
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: tbx6−/− and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− have a slightly weaker axial phenotype than her1−/−;her7−/−, which is preceded by a greater reduction of myotome boundaries.
source: whereas tbx6−/− and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− have a slightly weaker axial phenotype, which is preceded by a greater reduction of myotome boundaries.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: The similarities in paraxial and axial phenotypes of tbx6−/− and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− is explained by proposing that the effects of a disrupted segmentation clock are reduced in her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− by removing the output function of tbx6 in the anterior PSM.
source: The similarities in paraxial and axial phenotypes of tbx6−/− and her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− is explained by proposing that the effects of a disrupted segmentation clock (that can nevertheless output a disrupted pattern seen in her1−/−;her7−/−) are reduced in her1−/−;her7−/−;tbx6−/− by removing the output function of tbx6 in the anterior PSM.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The occasional defects in the mutant centra are attributed to the effects of fluctuations in the strength and position of sinks for the inhibitor component of the notochord's intrinsic segmentation mechanism.
source: We have attributed the occasional defects in the mutant centra to the effects of fluctuations in the strength and position of sinks for the inhibitor component of the notochord's intrinsic segmentation mechanism.
evidence: This is an inference based on the theoretical model.

claim: In the absence of any sinks, the notochord would in the model segment without any defects with a periodicity determined entirely by the internal dynamics.
source: In the absence of any sinks, the notochord would in our model segment without any defects with a periodicity determined entirely by the internal dynamics.
evidence: This is a prediction from the theoretical model.

claim: The defects can be viewed as a 'dominant interference' by the mis-patterned paraxial mesoderm.
source: Thus, the defects can be viewed as a 'dominant interference' by the mis-patterned paraxial mesoderm.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the theoretical model.

claim: It appears highly unlikely that her1, her7 and tbx6 are expressed in the notochord and may be directly responsible for the centra defects seen in the mutants.
source: We have also contemplated the possibility that her1, her7 and tbx6 are also expressed in the notochord and may be directly responsible for the centra defects seen in the mutants. However, this appears highly unlikely, because no tbx6 (Wanglar et al., 2014), mespb or her1 expression (In situ hybridization or transgene expression at 5 dpf and 13 dpf, data not shown) has been detected in the notochord at somite stages or during chordacentra formation.
evidence: This is an inference based on data from the study and a citation to previous research.

claim: Overexpression of mespbb in the notochord sheath can regulate segment size, possibly via interfering with boundary formation.
source: A recent report indicates that overexpression of mespbb in the notochord sheath can regulate segment size, possibly via interfering with boundary formation (Wopat et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Since the notochord's segments are generated over a long time scale, with a period about 20 times slower than somitogenesis, it seems plausible that the large molecular numbers that could be synthesized in this interval could ensure a low error rate.
source: While any molecular patterning mechanism would be vulnerable to fluctuations in the embryo, since the notochord's segments are generated over a long time scale, with a period about 20 times slower than somitogenesis, it seems plausible that the large molecular numbers that could be synthesized in this interval could ensure a low error rate.
evidence: This is speculation based on reasoning about molecular dynamics.

claim: The transfer of information from a segmentation clock-derived muscle pre-pattern to an autonomous but plastic mechanism in the notochord resolves the apparent discrepancy between tbx6 and hes6 mutant phenotypes.
source: Furthermore, the transfer of information from a segmentation clock-derived muscle pre-pattern to an autonomous but plastic mechanism in the notochord resolves the apparent discrepancy between tbx6 and hes6 mutant phenotypes
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations and the proposed model.

claim: The transfer of information from a segmentation clock-derived muscle pre-pattern to an autonomous but plastic mechanism in the notochord explains how the animal coordinates segmented muscles and axial skeleton in biomechanical register despite the fact that they develop days to weeks apart in time.
source: and explains how the animal coordinates segmented muscles and axial skeleton in biomechanical register despite the fact that they develop days to weeks apart in time.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations and the proposed model.

claim: Such a coordination mechanism may be a widespread feature of the teleosts and potentially other vertebrates.
source: Such a coordination mechanism may be a widespread feature of the teleosts and potentially other vertebrates.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings of the study.

claim: The genetic basis of the proposed autonomous notochord mechanism and the signal from myotome to notochord are not understood.
source: The genetic basis of the proposed autonomous notochord mechanism and the signal from myotome to notochord are not understood
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: Understanding the control of entpd5 expression may hold the key to understanding the autonomous notochord mechanism.
source: entpd5 is the earliest known molecular marker for the sites of ossification, with plasticity in the presence of perturbation, suggesting that understanding the control of entpd5 expression may hold the key.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings of the study.

claim: All mutants had a greater variability in segment number than wild type.
source: All mutants had a greater variability in segment number than wild type (n = 48), where segment number ranged from 29 to 31.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: In her1−/−;her7−/− the segment number increased up to 37.
source: In her1−/−;her7−/− (n = 38) the segment number increased up to 37.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: The increase in segment number in her1;her7 was slightly ameliorated by the additional removal of tbx6 in the triple mutants.
source: The increase in her1;her7 was slightly ameliorated by the additional removal of tbx6 in the triple mutants (n = 47).
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: hes6 mutants had a lower number of segments than the wild type, ranging from 28 to 31 segments.
source: As expected, hes6 mutants (n = 41) had a lower number of segments than the wild type, ranging from 28 to 31 segments.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: her1−/−;her7−/− presented a higher frequency and a broader distribution of defects than tbx6 mutants.
source: When the same fish were scored for segmentation defects (Figure 7—figure supplement 9B), her1−/−;her7−/− presented a higher frequency and a broader distribution of defects than tbx6 mutants (n = 46).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: In her1;her7;tbx6 mutants, the number of defects per embryo decreased almost to the distribution seen in tbx6 mutants.
source: In her1;her7;tbx6 mutants, the number of defects per embryo decreased almost to the distribution seen in tbx6 mutants.
evidence: This is supported by data from the study.

claim: The trends in segment number and defect measurements are captured by the theory.
source: The trends in these measurements are captured by the theory, as shown by the number of peaks in the pattern and (Figure 7—figure supplement 9C) the number of defects (Figure 7—figure supplement 9D), defined as segments of lengths outside the wild type segment length range.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of theoretical predictions to experimental data shown in figures.

claim: In the simulations of the wild type, there is always a correspondence between the position of the sink and the position of the peak of activator.
source: In the simulations of the wild type, there is always a correspondence between the position of the sink and the position of the peak of activator (Figure 7B and E)
evidence: This is a result from the theoretical model shown in figures.

claim: In experimental wild type animals, there is a correspondence between the positions of the myotome boundary and the entpd5 expression ring.
source: this situation is also found between the positions of the myotome boundary and the entpd5 expression ring in experimental wild type animals (Figure 7—figure supplement 8A–F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: In the simulations of tbx6, her1;her7 and her1;her7;tbx6 mutants, the strict correspondence between sink and activator is lost.
source: In the simulations of tbx6, her1;her7 and her1;her7;tbx6 mutants this strict correspondence between sink and activator is lost (Figure 7C and D); activator peaks occur both together with sinks and in between them.
evidence: This is a result from the theoretical model shown in figures.

claim: The disorganized myotome boundary fragments in the mutants had lost strict correspondence with the entpd5 rings.
source: We observed that the disorganized myotome boundary fragments in the mutants had lost strict correspondence with the entpd5 rings (Figure 7—figure supplement 8G–R).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The lack of spatial correspondence between paraxial structure and axial expression is in agreement with the model, and it supports the hypothesis that the sink is associated with some feature of the myotome boundary.
source: This lack of spatial correspondence between paraxial structure and axial expression is in agreement with the model, and it supports the hypothesis that the sink is associated with some feature of the myotome boundary.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the model predictions to experimental data.

claim: The theory is capable of autonomous pattern formation in the absence of sinks.
source: Thus, the theory proposed is capable of autonomous patterning of the notochord in the absence of input from the segmentation clock.
evidence: This is a result from the theoretical model.

claim: The system is able to form a pattern sequentially, from anterior to posterior, starting from a small perturbation in the anterior.
source: Starting from such a small perturbation in the anterior, we observe that the system is able to form a pattern sequentially, from anterior to posterior, see Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 2 and Video 1.
evidence: This is a result from the theoretical model shown in figures and videos.
